pass_b_english: The cornerstone of our faith is honorable, and those who believe in him will not be put to shame, as it is written in Scripture (1 Peter 2:6).
Paul, our divine messenger, understood this concept very well, and as a wise master builder, he laid a foundation, teaching us about the importance of a strong base.
For no one can lay another foundation except the one that is laid, which is Jesus Christ, the foundation of our faith, as stated in 1 Corinthians 3:11.

Therefore, having the Lord Jesus Christ as the foundation and cornerstone of true knowledge of God, we hold fast to our confession, examining our own heart, lest some unbelief escapes our notice, as warned in Hebrews 12:15, and we examine our own heart.
Lest some root of bitterness spring up and cause trouble, according to what is written, and lead us astray from the path of righteousness.

For the evil thing, the incurable disease, seems to be the double-mindedness, which is the most shameful of all things, and those who are in this state do not suffer willingly, and it would not be wrong to say that it is the most shameful of all things.
For it is easy to fall into this weakness, and one can see a house that has fallen from its foundation, easily destroyed, just like a soul that has lost its way.

In the same way, one can see Satan tempting the human soul, if, having abandoned the foundation, that is, Christ, and being double-minded, it is taken captive by deceit, and thus it would be taken captive.
It seems to me that a disciple of Christ should speak correctly and without reproach about such people, that it would have been better for them not to have known the way of truth.
For it has happened to them as in the true Proverb, a dog returns to its own vomit, and a pig, after being washed, returns to wallowing in the mud, as stated in 2 Peter 2:22.

It is utterly disgusting, brothers, to see an unclean dog returning to its own vomit, and similarly, one who has turned back to their former ways will be condemned, and it is a long and ugly thing, and a pig, after being washed, returns to wallowing in the mud, and it is a long and ugly thing.
It is shameful and absurd to speak of those who have turned back to their former ignorance and unbelief, having previously been cured of the disease of unbelief through faith in Christ.

A certain doctor healed the passion using discoveries from his skill, turning it to gentleness, and soothing the worst part of the evil, but who, having fallen into foolishness, would be taken captive, and it would not be wrong to say that it is the most shameful of all things.

Since it is not the earthly body, but the most powerful soul and mind that have been freed from ancient and miserable thoughts, and we have passed through the disease of politics, and we have examined our own heart, and we have passed through the disease of politics.

And will someone, having mixed everything up, appear and speak a cold word from the heart, and what kind of harm will it bring to us to believe in one father and creator of all things, but to distribute honors also to the worldly demons, thrones, powers, and dominions, and to the holy and God-inspired scripture itself?

It is fitting to say again that it is unbelievable and completely without sound, and even dangerous, to attempt to crown with equal and measured honors, and to envy the one who seeks the earthly kingdom, and those who are under his feet, and have bowed their necks to him as a slave.

For it is not the case that ruling all things is a special privilege for those who have obtained it, but rather it seems that some people think that being subordinate to others is harmonious; however, I think no one is in doubt about the fact that true power comes from God.

And if some of those who have been appointed as subjects are well-disposed and genuine, they will be worthy of respect and glory, but if they are disobedient and ill-tempered, they will be ranked among the most hostile, and they will receive the ultimate justice, according to their deeds.

Nevertheless, it is necessary to examine this matter, and to consider the nature of true authority, and I would say that it is a sign of excellent judgment to be able to see clearly that even those who have obtained genuine glory and are testified to through their actions, sometimes have a share of good reputation and the highest honor, not from their own home or from their own authority, but from the voluntary inclination of the ruler.

And the source of all honor and glory is the will of the king, who is the ultimate authority, and those who receive honors are not those who have them naturally, but those who accept them, and are humble enough to recognize their place.

As long as they think correctly about the king's things, they have a stable power and are in good repute, and their position is secure, but if they turn to the opposite, they will no longer be envied, but will fall into misery and extreme evil, and their downfall will be swift.

And if someone were to devise wicked plans and, driven by unbridled madness, were to rebel and, rashly seizing arms and tyrannical pursuits, were to destroy cities and countries, and, having thrown the necessary yoke on some, were to force the glory of the kingdom upon himself, it would be among the sober, not because of this to be honored, but not even with those ruling all will it be arranged, for true power comes from God alone.

Much is needed, in terms of wisdom and discernment, to navigate the complexities of power and authority, and having been done, rather the words of foolishness and the undertakings of the impious would be requested, and very likely, equal and similar punishment.

But let this be said and understood from our own matters, as if written on a tablet, for the sake of clarity and remembrance, and let us consider the divine, beautiful and sharp-sighted, and the queen of all, according to the inherent nature, and her ineffable power and authority.

For there is one Master of all, and Creator, and Lord of all, who is the source of all power and authority, as stated in Colossians 1:16, and since He is good by nature, in order that this might not be known only to Him, but also to others, He brought into being the things that did not exist, and established the order of creation.

And He created a multitude of holy spirits, greater in number, to serve and worship Him, and to carry out His will, and He established the best order for the things that have come into being, and named some Beginning, and Lordship, and Throne, and some Archangels, and Angels, each with their own role and function.

For He thinks nothing else than what He has, well and blamelessly, in every way and always, and has measured out the honor that seems to Him alone to each of the things that have come into being, according to His wisdom and justice.

The multitude of holy angels in heaven is countless, with certain Archai and Exousiai and Thrones established by God, filling the role of a father or teacher to the others, and things were thus, and not otherwise, from the beginning, and the order of creation has been established by God Himself.

When you hear the sacred Scriptures mentioning Dynamis and Thrones and Kyriotetes, do not suppose a multitude of gods is being proclaimed, but rather the various ranks and orders of angels and heavenly beings, and do not be led astray by ignorance, neglecting the doctrines of truth.

As the blessed Paul writes, one God is the creator and Lord of all, and there is no other, as stated in the Scriptures, and myriads of holy angels stand before Him, worshiping and serving Him, and carrying out His will, as part of the heavenly host.

Everything that has come into being through Him bears the yoke of servitude, and is subject to His authority, as the Creator and Lord of all, as stated in Psalm 103:19, and if some have rebelled and been punished, they have fallen.
Having fallen from the highest city, they have led some on earth astray, trying to seize God's glory for themselves, one of whom was the first.

The word of God says, 'A dog returns to its own vomit, and a pig, after being washed, returns to wallowing in the mud' (2 Peter 2:22), and 'It would have been better for them not to have known the way of truth, or having known it, to turn back to what was handed down to them as a holy commandment' (2 Peter 2:21).
